Security architecture

Explicit permissions, modest claims.

PEACOCK has layered capability checks and resource budgets; it is not a kernel-enforced sandbox or audited security product.

A layered capability model

Authority must be declared by source, checked by the VM and granted by the host.

Implemented

Static declarations

Protected native calls require the enclosing function to declare the corresponding capability.

Independent

Host grants

`--grant fs`, `compute` or `ui` is separate from a source declaration; grants do not leak between VM instances.

Best effort

Filesystem policy

Path traversal, absolute path and symlink escapes are rejected; `fs.create_dir` is sandbox-rooted.

Implemented subset

Resource budgets

VM steps, call depth, output, tensor elements, dataset samples and training epochs are limited.

Not an OS sandbox

Threat boundary

Python owns process memory and filesystem syscalls. TOCTOU and hostile-host risks are documented; no formal isolation claim is made.

Capability example

Selectable source — use your browser's copy command. · SHA-256: 02e322717ef5ec2e

use fs
fn main() -> Unit {
    capability fs;
    fs.create_dir("generated/site");
    fs.write_text("generated/site/index.txt", "hello");
}

Responsible vulnerability reporting

Do not include secrets or exploit payloads in a public issue. Follow the repository security policy for private reports.
